description:
Record a technical action in the turn log (an attack, a spell, a check, using an ability). `mode` — your intent: CREATE — a new action (its textId is not yet taken in this pass); UPDATE — supplement your own action of this pass by `action.textId` (fill in `result` from the numbers seen, add damage after a hit, fix the description or movement). A missed intent is an error with no record: CREATE on a taken textId, UPDATE on a nonexistent one. The first line of the response names the branch.
        |🎲 THE SERVER ROLLS THE DICE: in `rolls` send only SPECIFICATIONS (description, roller, diceType, count, rollType, modifiers, dc/dcSource) — the server will roll and return the action with the actual results/total in this same tool-result. Sending results is impossible: they are not in the schema.
        |⏳ YOU WILL SEE THE NUMBERS ONLY IN YOUR NEXT RESPONSE: the tool-result arrives AFTER the end of this response, so right now the roll's outcome does not exist either for you or in the description. Do not describe the outcome in the text and do NOT fill in `result` in the same response in which you roll — that is invention before resolution (live turns: four failures in a row were played out as successes); fill it in on the next pass (mode=UPDATE), having seen total against the DC. Filling in `result` from numbers ALREADY SEEN — on the contrary, is exactly this work. Deducting a resource/charge — on the contrary, goes BEFORE the roll in this same response: it does not depend on the outcome.
        |⚔️ An attack with damage — in ONE call: slot 0 — the attack (dc=target AC, dcSource=TARGET), slot 1 — damage with `onlyIf="hit(0)"` — the server will roll damage ONLY on a hit (natural 20/natural 1 accounted for; a non-standard crit threshold — `hit(0, 19)`). A skipped slot will come back marked "not rolled".
        |🎯 AoE / SEVERAL TARGETS with one spell (an area save spell) — also ONE action: `targets` — all the targets. In `rolls`: a saving-throw slot for EACH target (`roller` and `targets` — this target; `dc` — the actor's DC, `dcSource=ACTOR`; the target's modifiers) and ONE damage slot for all (`roller` — the actor, `targets` — those who receive damage; the dice are rolled once). Do NOT split an AoE into separate actions per target.
        |Then work from the actual numbers: a crit (natural 20) → add the DOUBLING of the damage dice by a spec AT THE END of `rolls` (mode=UPDATE) and mark "critical" in result; ALL damage dice are doubled, including the slot's DICE modifiers (sneak/smite etc.) — static bonuses once. `result` — only a substantive outcome: the "success/failure" verdict and the roll numbers are NOT written into it (they are read from dc/total), a check without consequences — result is empty.
        |🎲➕ A BONUS DIE INSIDE a roll (a random bonus: Guidance/Bless/Bardic Inspiration on a check or attack; mixed damage: 1d8 weapon + 2d6 sneak) is NOT a separate roll but a COMPONENT of the same slot: add it to `modifiers` next to the static ones, giving it a `diceType` (for 2d6 — also `count:2`) and a caption, WITHOUT value. A check example: a d20 slot with modifiers=[{description:'Prof',value:3},{description:'Guidance',diceType:D4}] → the server will roll a d4 and return "d20: 8 | +3 Prof | 🎲d4: 4 Guidance = 15 vs DC 15 ✓". A damage example: a weapon d8 slot + modifier {description:'Sneak Attack',diceType:D6,count:2}. The server rolls the bonus die itself and includes it in total — the roll line is self-sufficient for its own check. Do NOT move Guidance/sneak into a SEPARATE roll. For a pinned slot the dice component's value is the server's — do not repeat it.
        |🎲 Pinned textId slots (rolled or skipped by onlyIf; they survive removeAction too) are CANON: the dice, the roller, the targets, the description and other authored fields do not change, a reroll/overwrite is impossible. If you are not adding rolls — do not send `rolls` (the slots stay as they were). If you are adding (and on CREATE of the same textId after removeAction) — first repeat ALL pinned slots as shown (do not repeat server fields), then the new ones; a list shorter than the pinned ones is an error; you cannot insert a new slot between pinned ones.
        |✏️ Fields on mode=UPDATE: not sent — stays as it was (`targets`, `result`, `icon`, `rationale`, `movement`); what is sent replaces; to erase `result`/`icon` — an empty string. `targets`: the list REPLACES all targets and must include the targets of pinned slots; [] — no targets. On CREATE `targets` not sent or [] — no targets.
        |📌 The canon of the first declaration — mode=UPDATE does NOT change it: the frame (`frameId` — do not send or repeat the same), the cost (`resourceCosts` — do not send or repeat the same; for an action without a cost a sent one is the first declaration and is deducted), the movement length (`movement.feet` — do not send or repeat the same; for an action without movement feet is not sent). A different value — an error. To change them — removeAction (the deducted cost will return to the sheet) and mode=CREATE anew with the same textId and the needed values; repeat the pinned slots first.
        |Format movement with the `movement` field (from/to, the mode — its mode field) — coordinates are not written in description.
name: addAction

mode.description: CREATE — a new action (the textId is not yet taken in this pass); UPDATE — supplement an existing action of this pass by action.textId

textId.description: Stable slug identifier of the action within the turn (`[a-z0-9-]+`, for example 'attack-sword-zalrir'). The planner sets it in the task description, the implementor uses it — server rolls and the place in the feed (frameId, below) are bound to it ([FEED-LEGACY] — the same slug on `parts[].actionTextId`). (required, must not be empty)

frameId.description: Address of the parent frame (`p3`) — the one addPart returned. The action and everything it changed in the world become children of THIS narrative frame (the feed's parent). Only a part that tells about the world (STORY/LOCATION/REACTION/EPILOGUE) can be a frame — META/CHOICE/PLAYER_META_QUESTION/HISTORY/MEMORY do not qualify as an address. Take it from the parts added by YOUR addPart in THIS SAME contribution — until the first such frame there can be no action.

description.description: Short description of the action (for example: 'Sword attack', 'Spell'). Movement coordinates are NOT written here — the movement field is for them.

actor.description: Who performs the action: a game character (character) or a non-character — a trap, a collapse, the environment (nonCharacter).

character.description: Game character: textId from the roster (preferred) or the exact name. Exactly one of character/nonCharacter.

targets.description: Targets of the action (for an area — all affected in one list); each is of the same kind as actor. mode=UPDATE: do not send the field — the targets stay as they were; send a list — it replaces ALL targets (pinned slots require their targets to be in the list); [] — no targets. mode=CREATE: do not send or [] — no targets.

character.description: Game character: textId from the roster (preferred) or the exact name. Exactly one of character/nonCharacter.

result.description: The substantive outcome not visible from the dice: damage ('5 piercing damage'), an effect ('entangled, speed 0'), a consequence ('the door is forced open'). Do NOT duplicate the success/failure verdict and the roll numbers — they are read from dc/total. With no consequences — leave null. No artistic description.

rationale.description: Check rationale: the player's stated APPROACH → skill, and what is at stake. REQUIRED for actions with a d20 roll (attack — briefly: weapon → target AC). If you cannot formulate it — no roll is needed.

rolls.description: Roll specifications of this action in order. The pinned slots of this action (rolled by the server or skipped by onlyIf; shown in the tool's response and in the snapshot) repeat FIRST, as shown: the dice, the roller, the targets, the description and other authored fields are canon; the server fields (the server group in the form: results, total, the value of dice modifiers, etc.) do not repeat. NEW slots — after the pinned ones. You cannot insert a new slot between pinned ones, remove or reorder a pinned one.

diceType.description: Die type (D4, D6, D8, D10, D12, D20, D100)

count.description: Number of dice of this type (2d6 → diceType=D6, count=2). For checks/attacks — 1.

rollType.description: Roll type (normal, with advantage, with disadvantage)

advantageSource.description: Source of the advantage or disadvantage

modifiers.description: Roll modifiers (skill/attack bonuses with labels — you compute them from the character sheet and circumstances)

description.description: Description of the modifier / bonus component (for example 'Prof', 'Strength', 'Guidance', 'Sneak Attack')

value.description: Value of a STATIC modifier (a flat bonus: +3 proficiency, +2 Strength). For a DICE component (diceType is set) do NOT fill in — the server will roll the die and write the rolled sum here (as a tool this is a server field: do not repeat it for a pinned slot).

diceType.description: Type of the bonus DIE, if this component is a die roll INSIDE a check/attack/damage (Guidance/Bless d4, Bardic Inspiration, sneak damage 2d6): D4/D6/D8/D10/D12/D20/D100. Set ONLY when the bonus is random. null — an ordinary static modifier (a flat number in value).

count.description: Number of bonus dice (2d6 sneak → diceType=D6, count=2). 1 by default. Meaningful only together with diceType.

dc.description: Roll success threshold: the check/saving throw DC or the target's AC for an attack (total >= dc — success). REQUIRED for d20 rolls with a STATIC threshold; null — the roll has no threshold (damage, initiative, pure randomness). For a contested check do NOT fill in — use dcFromRoll.

dcFromRoll.description: CONTESTED check (Charisma against Wisdom, etc.): the index of the OPPOSING roll in rolls of THIS SAME action. Declare both rolls as elements of rolls; the server will roll both and substitute the opposing result into this roll's dc (a tie = the status quo, the initiator succeeds only by exceeding). Mutually exclusive with an explicit dc.

roller.description: Who rolls this die — REQUIRED for every roll, there is no default. Attack, damage, check — the one performing it; saving throw — the target who makes it.

character.description: Game character: textId from the roster (preferred) or the exact name. Exactly one of character/nonCharacter.

targets.description: Targets of THIS roll — a subset of the action's targets. Required if the action has more than one target; empty — the action's only target. Area damage in total is ONE roll with a list of recipients; a saving throw — one slot per target.

character.description: Game character: textId from the roster (preferred) or the exact name. Exactly one of character/nonCharacter.

dcSource.description: Whose threshold dc is — REQUIRED when dc is set: TARGET — a property of the target (AC for an attack); ACTOR — a property of the actor (the DC of their spell: for a saving throw the roller is the target, while the threshold is the actor's); MASTER — assigned by the master (check DC, environment, trap). Not needed with dcFromRoll.

onlyIf.description: Roll CONDITION (a CEL expression): the slot is rolled only if the condition is true given the ALREADY rolled previous slots. The main case — attack damage: onlyIf="hit(0)" (the damage roll only on a hit of slot 0). hit(i) accounts for a natural 20 (auto-hit) and a natural 1 (auto-miss); a non-standard crit threshold — hit(0, 19) (Champion 19-20). Available: hit(i), hit(i, critFrom), miss(i), miss(i, critFrom), rolls[i].raw/total/dc. You may reference only PREVIOUS slots. null — always rolled.

transform.description: Outcome TRANSFORM (a CEL expression, evaluated AFTER the roll): adjusts the canonical total of the slot. The main case — half damage when the SINGLE victim holds (half-on-success, one target): transform="halfIf(hit(0))" (slot 0 is this target's saving throw; half rounded down — as in D&D). The slot's outcome is one for all its targets: on shared damage across several targets transform is inapplicable. Available: halfIf(cond), total/raw/dc of THIS roll + rolls[i] and hit/miss of the previous ones (full form: "hit(0) ? total / 2 : total"). null — the outcome is not adjusted.

movement.description: Structured movement, if the action involves movement across the map (move/dash/teleport or movement before an attack).

from.description: Map cell BEFORE the movement (the token's current position from mapPlacement)

x.description: X coordinate on the battle map (in cells)

y.description: Y coordinate on the battle map (in cells)

x.description: X coordinate on the battle map (in cells)

y.description: Y coordinate on the battle map (in cells)

mode.description: Mode: WALK — ordinary movement within speed; DASH — a dash (spends an action, budget ×2); FORCED — involuntary (a push, a pull, a fall); TELEPORT — teleportation (Misty Step etc., the path is not checked)

feet.description: Length of the actual path in feet accounting for difficult terrain (cells × the map's cellSizeFeet, difficult terrain ×2). For TELEPORT — the straight-line distance.

mover.description: Who moves; the actor by default. Required for FORCED: the pushed target from the action's targets.

character.description: Game character: textId from the roster (preferred) or the exact name. Exactly one of character/nonCharacter.

resourceCosts.description: The action's cost as sheet rows: a resourceId from the actor's resources[] + a quantity. The ONLY channel for spending paid for by the action: everything declared here is deducted by the server itself — do NOT deduct the same by a gesture on the sheet (it would be deducted twice). A spent economy slot — action/bonus_action/reaction (1) and movement (feet walked) — put here; deducted as declared, without refusal (the remainder may go negative — you sort out the overspend on the sheet). Other resources (spell_slot_N slots, ki, charges, ammunition): the resource EXISTS but there is not enough — refusal; the resource is NOT on the sheet — a warning with a list of available ones, the action goes through, there is nothing to deduct.

resourceId.description: textId of a resource from the actor's resources[] (for example 'pact-magic-slots', 'ki-points').

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description:
Add a long-term memory record to a character (PC or NPC). The memory lives in the sheet itself, survives history compaction (chapters), and is always visible to the planner and the implementors in subsequent turns.

        |The types (`type`) are mutually exclusive, choose exactly one by content:
        |- `EVENT` — a one-time plot event that happened and left a mark (the death of a loved one, an escape from captivity, found an artifact, survived a catastrophe). This is "a fact of what happened". Not for relationships (RELATIONSHIP) and not for information (KNOWLEDGE).
        |- `RELATIONSHIP` — a lasting relationship with a **specific** other character (ally/enemy/mentor/lover/debtor/blood enemy/rival). Exists over time. A shift in the relationship per the plot is a new understanding: close the previous record and write a new one under a new `memoryTextId`. Do not confuse with IMPRESSION (a one-off assessment).
        |- `OBLIGATION` — an **INTERNAL** oath, vow, a personal promise to oneself or loved ones. The source is **inside** the character. No outside employer, no reward from outside. **Do not confuse with QUEST**: if there is someone who hired/commissioned/asked from outside — it is a QUEST, not an OBLIGATION.
        |- `KNOWLEDGE` — learned information (a secret, a fact, a rumor, a name, a location, a secret). "What the character now knows". Do not confuse with EVENT (there it is an event; here it is information).
        |- `REPUTATION` — a **group** opinion of the character in a faction/location/guild/layer of society. Do not confuse with IMPRESSION (the opinion of one NPC).
        |- `IMPRESSION` — **FOR NPCs ONLY**. The subjective impression of **one** NPC about someone/something: a PC, **another NPC**, a place, a faction, an event. NPC↔NPC impressions are just as important: they make the world alive (NPCs react to each other in scenes — ally, dislike, despise). Not allowed for a PC — an error will be returned. `directive` is especially important — it literally dictates the NPC's behavior.
        |- `QUEST` — an **EXTERNAL** contract, hire, commission from a client (an NPC, a guild, a faction, a note). Usually there is a goal and a reward. The UI separately shows the active QUEST as a counter on the character's portrait. **Any paid work of a PC = QUEST.**

        |Edge cases:
        |- A PC swore to avenge their parents themself → OBLIGATION. A PC hired by a merchant to find the killers for money → QUEST.
        |- A PC's first meeting with an NPC → IMPRESSION (for the NPC). When the relationship has already been established over time → RELATIONSHIP as a separate record under a new `memoryTextId`, close the previous IMPRESSION as `OUTDATED`.
        |- A MILESTONE / progress on a quest (a stage on the way to the goal: reached the place, defeated the guardian, found the key) is NOT closing the quest. Record the milestone with a SEPARATE EVENT with a `RELATES_TO` link to the QUEST record; do NOT touch the quest's own status. A QUEST is moved to COMPLETED (via updateMemory) ONLY when its goal's wording itself has been achieved, not an intermediate victory.

        |Gesture and id. `addMemory` — "the character remembered something new": new knowledge and new understanding are written only under a NEW `memoryTextId`. If the understanding changed per the plot (a rumor turned out false, an impression changed, a deal was terminated) — close the previous record (`updateMemory` with `status=OUTDATED` and `outcome`, or via the new one's `closes` parameter) and write a new one. An existing id (including that of a lifted record) is rejected: refining the same record and returning a lifted one — via `updateMemory`.

        |Fields:
        |- `fact` — what happened objectively, without emotions. At least 20 characters.
        |- `context` — the personal meaning for **this** character: emotions, assessment, with whom they are ready to share, secrecy. In their voice in the first person. If the context is personal — explicitly mark "does not share with the first person they meet" or "only with X", otherwise the narrative agent may blurt it out.
        |- `directive` (optional) — **FOR NPCs ONLY**. A behavioral stance for the NPC in future turns. For a PC — null (controlled by a live player).
        |- `importance` — LOW/NORMAL/HIGH, for resolving contradictions between directives.
name: addMemory

type.description: Memory type. IMPRESSION — for NPCs only.

fact.description: Objective fact (no emotions, no interpretation). At least 20 characters.

directive.description: Optional, for NPCs ONLY: a behavioral stance. For a PC pass null.

atRound.description: Round number when the event happened. For events of the current turn — take `currentRoundNumber` from CURRENT GAME STATE. For backstory/events before the game starts — 0. Do NOT leave 1 by default.

subjectTextId.description: Optional: textId of the character the record is about (for IMPRESSION/RELATIONSHIP — be sure to set it). Used only for UI grouping.

closes.description: Optional: textIds of memory records of THIS SAME character that this record CLOSES (chain consolidation: list EVERY original). Each target automatically becomes OUTDATED. To close use THIS parameter, not links.

description:
Add a new character state (Blinded, Poisoned, Bear Transformation, Concentration on a spell, etc.).
        |⏳ The state's timer is in SECONDS of game time (durationSeconds): round = 6, minute = 60, hour = 3600. The server immediately stamps the moment of staleness (expiresAtClock) IN THE CARRIER'S TIME — "for an hour" means an hour of THEIR time, and spells tick in battle and out of it alike.
        |⛔ A STATE MUST HAVE AN END. When setting a state, you must answer HOW IT WILL END, and record the answer in exactly one of two ways (both is allowed):
        |  • a DEADLINE — `durationSeconds` (invisibility for 1 hour → 3600, a blessing for 10 rounds → 60). The server stamps the moment of staleness, and then the state is removed by the clock;
        |  • a TRIGGER — the end condition IN WORDS in `duration`: "fades when the character attacks or casts", "until concentration ends", "until a long rest", "while holding the torch". The trigger must be verifiable by the playing out, not "while in effect".
        |A spell/potion/ability effect WITHOUT both is a defect: such a state will hang on the character forever, and no scene master will remove it. An empty deadline AND trigger are legal ONLY for a substantively PERMANENT state (a curse until removed by a ritual, an innate trait, a maiming, a cult mark) — and then write exactly that in `duration` ("permanent, until removed by a ritual").
        |⛔ The SECRET `secret` is REQUIRED at the birth of a state, there is no default: "all" — public, visible to the player; "nobody" — hidden, nobody knows except the carrier; a list of UUIDs — exactly they know.
        |If a state with that stateId already exists — an error: change it with `updateState`, remove with `removeState`, and only then set anew. When it ended — remove with `removeState` and play out the ending in the narrative.

description:
Update an existing memory. Use for:
        |- Refining the fact/context/directive of the same record (details were added, the wording was corrected). If the understanding changed per the plot — not here: close the record (`OUTDATED`) and write a new one via `addMemory` under a new `memoryTextId`.
        |- **Fixing a wrongly chosen type (`type`).** Changing `type` is only a fix of a selection mistake: the record described from the very beginning the same thing as now, and the type was chosen wrongly. If the record became different because something happened after it (a rumor was confirmed, a meeting grew into a relationship, a secret gave rise to a vow, an act changed the attitude of those around), — that is a new understanding: close the old one (`OUTDATED`) and write a new one of the right type via `addMemory` under a new id. The test — compare with the moment of writing: a type that was correct **at the moment of writing** differs from the recorded one — this is a selection mistake, fix it with `updateMemory`. The type was correct at the moment of writing but became wrong because of **subsequent** events — this is a new memory via `addMemory`. The restrictions are the same as for addMemory: IMPRESSION only for NPCs; directive not for a PC.
        |- **Status changes (`status` + `outcome`)** in this turn: ACTIVE — active (this is how a lifted one is returned), COMPLETED — successfully, FAILED — failed, ABANDONED — withdrawn/refused, OUTDATED — the rumor/fact turned out false or lost relevance (this is how the previous understanding is closed before a new record).

        |⚠️ A MILESTONE ≠ CLOSURE. `status=COMPLETED` is set ONLY when the quest goal's wording ITSELF (fact) has been achieved: the quest "stop the ritual" is closed by the ritual being STOPPED, not by "reached the altar" / "the guardian is defeated" / "we stand at the threshold". Intermediate progress (a milestone, a stage, a local victory on the way to the goal) is NOT finalization: record it with a SEPARATE memory (a new EVENT with a RELATES_TO link to the quest), WITHOUT changing status. If you moved an active quest to COMPLETED on a milestone — the campaign's goal was silently closed with a fake outcome.

        |Pass only the fields that change. If you set a final status — be sure to give an outcome with a short description of the result ("The maps were handed to Crow, the reward received", "Crow refused to pay the remainder").

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description:
Update a previously recorded master's decision (by exact textId). Use to bring canonical numbers and wordings up to date (the total strength drain changed, a new interpretation of a disputed question appeared) and to RE-HANG the grounds (a new basedOn). Do not breed duplicates via addDecision — for an existing textId always use updateDecision.

        |Works on a HISTORY decision too (past turns, the chapter's canon): history is immutable, so editing a historical node becomes its NEW VERSION in this turn — unset fields are inherited from the previous version, the status is kept. This way a retcon does not erase graph edges. In an ADD-ON (a lite pass) editing the canon of past turns is unavailable — only your own nodes; a contradiction with the canon is not recorded on top — play out the request without this edit, leave the contradiction to the scene master for the future.
name: updateDecision

textId.description: textId of an existing decision — of this turn or of the story. If there is no decision anywhere — an error; use addDecision.

decision.description: New decision text (fully replaces the old one). Not set — the previous text is kept (you edit only the grounds/idea).

reason.description: New decision IDEA — WHY it exists, in one phrase (fully replaces the old one). Not set — the previous idea is kept.

basedOn.description: References to grounds: `decision:<textId>` — another decision (of this turn, the story or the chapter, any status); `move:<ref>` — a request/choice of the player of the CURRENT turn, addressed by the character's name or its textId; `action:<textId>` — a roll (action) of this turn or the story; `book:<textId>` — a book node; `part:<round>:<partId>` — a specific narration part (what the master said to the player: a promise, an NPC line, a scene detail), the part's address is visible in the parts snapshot. Parenthood is causal ("why it happened") or contextual ("where it was introduced"). Not set — the previous grounds are kept; an empty array — removes them.

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: CANCEL a sync point: the scheduled event has become IRRELEVANT and will no longer happen — "wolves attack at night in the forest", but the party spent the night in a tavern; "we leave through the yard", but a fight broke out in the yard. The world stops waiting for it, the address is freed (if they want it — you will set it again), the canceled point no longer travels in the context. ⛔ This is NOT `completeSyncPoint`: there the event HAPPENED and has an outcome, here it did NOT happen and there is no outcome. The participants' played-out contributions remain canon — Cleve stood up and walked to the door, and in the narrative he does not teleport back to the table; only the failed event itself is canceled. Cancel a point when its meaning is exhausted, NOT because of a scene relocation: the point's scope is shown in the list of open ones (`scope:`), a point with the scope "until the end of the game" survives a relocation. ⏳ The cancellation takes effect together with your work — and, like processing, survives escalation.
name: cancelSyncPoint

textId.description: Address of the point being released.

reason.description: WHY the event will no longer happen — to the point ("the party is spending the night in the tavern, nobody will go into the forest until morning", "the fight started earlier — the departure through the yard is canceled").

description: PROCESS a sync point: the event HAPPENED, the world no longer waits for it. One tool for all cases of a taken-place event, the difference is in the OUTCOME: "everyone arrived and it is played out" / "we waited for the event — it occurred" / "we did not wait, I release". The outcome is written RELATIVE to the point's `condition`: check against it and name HOW the condition resolved ("Borya cast Shield — the reaction is played out"), not "time to close". ⛔ If you release one who HAS NOT YET ARRIVED — DO NOT INVENT a decision, consent or line for them: the snapshot honestly marks which of the addressees has had NOT A SINGLE contribution yet (`joinSyncPoint` was not called for them) — there is nothing to lean on for such a one. Write the outcome FOR THE EVENT, not for the absent player ("the party crossed the bridge, Vasya lagged behind on the road"): the time reconciliation that the processing gives will itself bring them up to the point's moment, and they will pick up their line with the NEXT request — with the remainder they arrived with. The completeness of joins does not close the point by itself: the decision is always yours. ⛔ The event did NOT take place and will not take place — this is not processing, this is `cancelSyncPoint`: do not write "I cancel" here as an outcome, otherwise the world will remember the failed as happened. ⏳ Processing takes effect together with your work — and SURVIVES escalation (a terminal decision on a point is not thrown out together with the pass's draft, even if the pass itself is escalated as a full turn).
name: completeSyncPoint

textId.description: Address of the point being worked.

outcome.description: How the point's condition resolved: "everyone chose a path, the party crosses the bridge", "dawn has come", "Vasya did not answer — I let him go, the party leaves without him".

description: DECLARE A SYNC POINT — a new SCHEDULED EVENT: what will happen, WHEN (if the deadline is already known), with whom and under what condition. While the point is open, the scene does not move through it: participants play out their part up to its moment, and you play out the event itself when the moment has come. There can be several points at once — different events, different subgroups. ⛔ If the address is ALREADY TAKEN by an open point — a refusal, not an addition: this tool creates a NEW point and only it. If you want to fix an existing one — `setSyncPointDue`/`setSyncPointPlayers`/`setSyncPointTexts`, each changes exactly one thing. ⏱ `afterMinutes` — in how much game time the event OCCURS, counted FROM THE FURTHEST OF THIS POINT'S ADDRESSEES (there is no common world clock — each participant has their own time, and the point is set FORWARD so that it can be reached; the one who went furthest is already there, the others are on their way): 0 — right now (the fight begins), 480 — "in eight hours, at dawn". DO NOT SPECIFY if the deadline is NOT YET KNOWN — without a moment the point WAITS for a trigger ("scouts will return with news", "someone will find the entrance to the dungeon"), it is not a barrier: it holds nobody and does not ripen by itself, but stays in the context as an open wait. Once you learn the deadline — assign it with `setSyncPointDue`. The moment and `condition` are DIFFERENT things: the moment says WHEN the event approaches, the condition — under what circumstances it will happen at all ("wolves attack at night IN THE FOREST"). An event scheduled for midnight will not catch off guard those who do not sleep at midnight — that is the meaning of the moment. The moment works ON ITS OWN too: an event conditioned on nothing but the deadline has no condition at all. WHOSE axes these are and whether `condition` accepts a particular kind is stated in the kind's section in the point norms, not here. If it becomes clear the event will no longer happen (the party spent the night in a tavern) — cancel the point with `cancelSyncPoint`, do not close it with an outcome. ⏳ The declaration takes effect TOGETHER with your work — when the pass reaches the end and it goes to the player; escalation throws out the work, and with it the declared event.
name: declareSyncPoint

textId.description: Point address: slug [a-z0-9-]+ up to 64 characters, by the meaning of the event ('sp-path-choice', 'sp-ambush-reaction'). Already taken by an open point — the call will be REJECTED.

kind.description: Point kind — see the value descriptions. The point kind — which world event it stands for. Evt — a scheduled world event. Sre — the party's short rest (a halt). Lre — the party's long rest (a night's stay). Scc — a change of scenery: the party moves to another place. Ben — entering a battle; the same kind is used to bring reinforcements into a battle already under way. What stands behind each kind — what consequence processing it has, who processes it and what is NOT expected of you for this kind — is stated in the point rules, in the SECTION OF THIS KIND.

reason.description: WHY the world is waiting — in one phrase, to the point ("the party was ambushed", "at the fork a path must be chosen").

condition.description: WHAT must happen for the event to take place ("everyone declared the round's action", "the party is still in the forest"). A criterion — you will check against it, not "by feel". DO NOT SPECIFY if the event has no condition beyond the deadline itself — the moment works on its own.

afterMinutes.description: In how many GAME MINUTES the event occurs, counted from the FURTHEST OF THE ADDRESSEES (each has their own time; the one who has gone furthest ahead is the baseline). 0 — now (a battle, an immediate reaction); 60 — in an hour; 480 — in eight hours. DO NOT SPECIFY if there is no deadline yet: without a moment the point is a wait, not a barrier, it holds nobody; you will assign the time with `setSyncPointDue` once the condition has fired.

players.description: Whom it concerns: textIds of characters (NPCs allowed too). DO NOT SPECIFY at all if the event concerns everyone — the server will fill in the current roster of ACTING scene participants (both players and NPCs).

scope.description: The point's LIFETIME SCOPE. Scn (scene, the default) — the point expires on relocation: there is nothing left to wait for in the new scene. Gm (game) — the point lives until the end of the game, relocation does not touch it (the BB timeline, global events). DO NOT SPECIFY if the point is ordinary — the scene is almost always what is needed.

description: Carry the CURRENT request being played out THROUGH a sync point: you judged that this request leads the participant to its event, rather than living as a free line alongside it. ⏱ IMPORTANT ABOUT TIME: a request is played out EXACTLY UP TO the point's moment and not a minute further — nobody passes through the event. Was the request broader ("I go to the farmer", and the event is a quarter of an hour away)? Play out what fit, and NAME the unplayed in `remainder`: this text will reach whoever will play out the event itself, and the party will continue with what each arrived at the event with. Nothing left — do not specify `remainder`. ⛔ A participant is counted as HAVING REACHED the point not by the fact of this call but by their own time: while their hour is less than the event's moment, they keep going toward it — with their next requests. The one carried is ALWAYS the character of the request you are playing out in THIS pass — there is nothing to choose someone else with (the tool has no parameter for this: NPCs and other players are brought into the point by `declareSyncPoint`/`setSyncPointPlayers`, not by `joinSyncPoint` with someone else's request). ⏳ Takes effect TOGETHER with your work (the player's contribution and its binding to the point are saved as one piece); escalation throws out both the work and the binding — the request will go out as a full turn, and the point will stay waiting.
name: joinSyncPoint

remainder.description: What of the request did NOT fit before the moment of the event — in one phrase, as an action ("reach the farmer and talk to him"). Do not specify if the request was played out in full.

description: SET THE MOMENT of an already open sync point — it moves the event's DEADLINE, and only it: the addressee roster and the texts (reason/condition) stay the same. Use when you learned that the event will occur earlier or later than stated ("the ambush will be not in an hour but right now"); you cannot fix the reason or the roster with this tool — for that use `setSyncPointTexts`/`setSyncPointPlayers`. ⏱ `afterMinutes` is counted FROM THE SAME BASE as at declaration — from the furthest of this point's CURRENT addressees, not from the old moment: if you said 60 — the moment will stand an hour from the furthest addressee RIGHT NOW, whatever was named before.
name: setSyncPointDue

textId.description: Address of the open point (see the "SYNC POINTS" block).

afterMinutes.description: In how many GAME MINUTES the event now occurs, counted from the furthest of the point's current addressees. 0 — right now.

description: SET THE ADDRESSEES of an already open sync point — the list REPLACES the previous one ENTIRELY, it does NOT add to it: name ALL whom the point should concern after this call, including those who were already on the list and remain. The point's moment and texts do not change. Use to bring a new participant into a wait already under way ("another enemy has come up to the ambush") or to remove one who is no longer an addressee ("this one left the scene, no reason to wait for him") — both with the same call: name the resulting list.
name: setSyncPointPlayers

textId.description: Address of the open point (see the "SYNC POINTS" block).

players.description: The FULL list of addressees AFTER this call: textIds of characters (NPCs allowed too). Replaces the previous list entirely — name those who must stay as well.

description: REFINE THE TEXTS of an already open sync point — the reason (`reason`) and the condition (`condition`) together, in ONE decision: this is one pair of facts about the point, not two independent fields, and both parameters are required on every call (leave the condition empty if the event has none or its kind of conditions does not accept one — but name it empty, do not inherit it by silence). The point's moment and addressees do not change.
name: setSyncPointTexts

textId.description: Address of the open point (see the "SYNC POINTS" block).

reason.description: WHY the world is waiting — in one phrase, to the point.

condition.description: WHAT must happen for the event to take place. Empty — the event has no condition beyond its deadline.

description: ORDER A NEW FACE from the character specialist: the scene needed someone who is not yet in the game (an innkeeper, a guide, a random passerby, a messenger, a trio of bandits). You say WHO is needed and WHY the scene needs them; the sheet, stats, look and canonical address are assembled by the specialist — you do not create characters yourself. ⏳ There will be NO result in THIS response: the order is executed at the end of the response, the finished face will appear in the snapshot in the NEXT response (in the ordered scene with the chosen visibility) — and there you will play out their appearance BY NAME, place a token (updateToken) and give them a line. Do not invent their name and lines in advance and do not go into review in the same response: the transition into REVIEW will be rejected until the order has returned. A repeat call — a SECOND face, not a reminder. The specialist is entitled to DECLINE (the reason will come in the same snapshot) — then you decide: do without the new face or escalate. NOT via an order: returning to the scene someone who ALREADY exists in the game — call enterScene or transferScene according to their current presence.
name: orderNpc

anyOf.description: Canonical audience shortcut.
Non-empty list of canonical observer UUIDs.

role.description: Who this is to the scene — role/function in words: "innkeeper", "guard sergeant", "syndicate liaison".

order.description: The order in words: why the scene needs the face, what it is busy with, what stands out, what has already been said about it in the text. Self-sufficient — the scene specialist does not see it.

significance.description: SIGNIFICANCE — your decision, not the specialist's: BACKGROUND — an extra with no lines; MINOR — a passing face for this scene (an innkeeper, a messenger); MAJOR — a figure the story will keep dealing with; LEAD — a key face of the arc. Be STINGY: raising significance later is cheaper than paying for depth that turned out not to be needed (both the depth of the sheet and the level of the portrayal depend on it).

textIdHint.description: The BASE OF THE ADDRESS in Latin letters — a short role slug (`wandering-merchant`, `dock-foreman`). The server will pick a free address and return the actual one; Cyrillic cannot become an address, so without a hint the face gets a faceless `npc-2`.

name.description: Name, if it has ALREADY been heard in the scene or in the book. null — the specialist will invent a name.

props.description: CANONICAL PROPS AS A LIST — items that must end up in their inventory ("a tube with papers", "a warehouse key"): what is not in the sheet cannot be handed over, taken away or searched. Prose in the order text does not count — list them.

guidance.description: Recommendations: tone, origin, manner, role in the scene. Do not dictate mechanics (stats, hp, attacks) — that is the specialist's. null — nothing to add.

count.description: How many faces are needed. 1 — one face; the specialist will differentiate a series with distinctions on their own. The series cap is 8: more is several orders.

presence.description: Whether the face is OFF-FRAME: OFFSTAGE — it is NOT in the scene, it drives events from off-frame (a mentioned client, the addressee of a letter) — no token is placed; ONSTAGE — enters the scene right now.

description: ORDER a character SHEET edit from the specialist — everything that goes beyond the sheet's state: a new item/weapon/gear in the inventory (bought, found, gifted, broken, lost), a learned spell, a new ability or resource, a change of max hp/stats/level, money. You formulate the ORDER in plain words ("bought a longsword for 15 gp — add it to the inventory, deduct the coins"), the sheet is edited by the specialist per the rules: you do not write the sheet yourself. ⏳ There will be NO result in THIS response: the order is executed at the end of the response, and you will see the updated sheet in the snapshot in the NEXT response — and there you will play it out. Do not invent the outcome in advance and do not go into review in the same response: the transition into REVIEW will be rejected until the order has returned. A repeat call is a NEW order, not a reminder of the old one. The specialist is entitled to DECLINE (the reason will come in the same snapshot) — then you decide: play on without what was ordered or escalate. NOT via an order (these are your own tools): hp, resources/charges/consumables, states, presence in the scene.
name: orderSheetChange

characterTextId.description: textId of the character whose sheet we are editing (known to the game — including those not currently in frame, standby).

order.description: The order in words: WHAT to change in the sheet and WHY (what happened in the scene). Self-sufficient — the scene specialist does not see it.

description: 🎭 HAND OVER CONTROL of a PLAYER's character to the master: attaches a state, while alive the character is played by its agent (`passSpotlight` starts letting this PC through), and the player's own requests the server either accepts lifting the delegation (voluntary), or rejects with the reason from the state (not voluntary). WHEN: a game-mechanical effect by canon (madness, domination, possession — voluntary=false) OR a meta-request from the player themself "play for me / I will be away" (voluntary=true). ⛔ You cannot take the turn from a LIVE, playing player: the state is visible in their sheet and is judged by the review like any canon object — groundless delegation is a defective turn. An ordinary NPC does not need delegation: its turn is passed by the spotlight. Lift with `removeState('<character textId>', 'master-delegated-control')` or by durationSeconds expiring.
name: delegateControl

characterTextId.description: textId of the PLAYER's character whose control passes to you. PC only: for NPCs the control is already yours.

reason.description: The REASON in one phrase — it becomes the state description IN THE player's sheet and the frame for the agent who will act for the character ("madness from the creature's howl", "the player asked to be played for until evening"). Write per the facts of the scene, without meta jargon.

voluntary.description: true — AT THE PLAYER'S REQUEST (the person is away from the table, asked to be played for): their next request will lift the delegation by itself. false — GAME MECHANICS (madness, domination): the player's requests will be rejected until you lift the state or it expires.

anyOf.description: all — public state, nobody — nobody knows except the carrier.
Non-empty list of character UUIDs who know the state (the holder always knows).

durationSeconds.description: How long the delegation LASTS, in seconds of global game time (round=6, minute=60, hour=3600). For voluntary=false REQUIRED (involuntary delegation is always finite) and capped at 86400 sec (24 game hours) — it can be extended longer by a repeat delegateControl after expiry. For voluntary=true null is legal (until lifted by the returning player's request).

description: 🎭 Pass the turn to a scene participant — the one whose turn it now is in the scene. MECHANICS. An NPC (and a player's character under your control): their agent produces an INTENT (what the character does/says/wants) — the intent arrives in the NEXT response, and their turn will OPEN when you close the current one (`closeMove`). YOU play out this turn: the intent is a DECLARATION to the world, equal to a player's request, and the world answers it by the common rules, including with a refusal. You can pass to several — their turns will open in order, in the order of passing. For a CAPABLE PLAYER CHARACTER passing means something else: "your turn, we are waiting for you" — no generation, they will submit the request themselves, and the pass ends there. One participant — once: to one who already holds the spotlight it is not passed again; and to one who has already reached the moment the world is waiting for there is nothing to move with — the pass is rejected. THE NORM. First the world, then the player: first pass the turn to those who have something to do or say right now, play out their turns — and only then pass to the player (while others' turns are not played out, a pass to the player is rejected). Pass to an NPC so that the world CATCHES UP with the players, not outpaces them: the spotlight is the world's answer to what has already been done, not a push of the plot forward. Play out extras, passing lines and background YOURSELF, without the spotlight. TYPICAL CASES: an NPC was addressed — they answer with their own turn; an NPC decides in the player's presence (agrees, haggles, attacks); the scene has settled and the world has answered — "your turn" to the player. COUNTER-EXAMPLE: after passing to the player do not pass to anyone — the scene is already theirs. There is nobody left to move — just close the move, and the pass will end.
name: passSpotlight

characterTextId.description: textId of the scene participant to whom you hand the turn. An NPC — always; a player's character — ONLY if control over it has been delegated to you by a state (`delegateControl`): we do not play for a capable player, their turn belongs to them.

vector.description: VECTOR — 1-2 sentences about where the scene is looking: a direction, NOT a script and not an outcome. The intent grows from the character themself, the vector only hints at context ("the conversation hit the price", "he sees the player reaching for a weapon"). May be omitted, up to 400 characters.

description: 🔓 REVEAL SHEET SECTIONS: the characters you name in `to` from this moment know the specified sections of the `character` sheet in full (health, AC, skills, abilities, gear, bio). Until a section is revealed, someone else's sheet is known only to the extent of the header by game difficulty. This is the master's decision about KNOWLEDGE, not an edit of the sheet; you cannot hide it back, a repeat is harmless. WHEN: in the scene a character learned about another what the section gives. TYPICAL CASES: examined the wounds — health; saw the armor — armor_class; saw them in action — abilities; asked about the past — bio; everything at once — "all_sheet". Nobody to reveal to (the carrier is alone in the scene, `to` is only themself) — the tool's response is an error. On the character card the revealed will appear from the next pass.
name: revealSheetSections

character.description: UUID of the sheet carrier from the game's canonical roster. (format: uuid)

anyOf.description: all_sheet — all six sections of the sheet.
Non-empty list of sheet sections to reveal.
party — reveal to the player characters who are currently in the scene.
Non-empty list of character UUIDs to whom the sheet sections is revealed.

description: 🔓 REVEAL A STATE'S SECRET: the characters you name in `to` from this moment know that `character` has the state `state` (before that only the carrier and those to whom the secret was revealed at birth knew it). WHEN: in the scene the state became known — the carrier confessed, it was noticed, the wound/mark/curse was discovered. This is the master's decision about KNOWLEDGE, not an edit of the state: the state itself does not change. You can reveal only what is already on the carrier's sheet; you cannot hide it back. What was revealed in this turn you see in the tool's result immediately, and on the character card — from the next pass. Nobody to reveal to (the carrier is alone in the scene, `to` is only themself) — the tool's response is an error: name characters or "all".
name: revealStateSecret

character.description: UUID of the state carrier from the game's canonical roster. (format: uuid)

state.description: textId of the state in the carrier's sheet (the same name as in `addState`/`removeState`).

anyOf.description: all — reveal to everyone, party — reveal to the player characters who are currently in the scene.
Non-empty list of character UUIDs to whom the secret is revealed.

description:
Remove a participant FROM THE BATTLE — from the roster: from the next circle they are not an addressee of the ROUND point and receive no turns.
        |CIRCLE BOUNDARY: the removal takes effect at the circle boundary — until its end the one who dropped out is still listed in the roster; there is no need to hand a turn to the dead or to one who left the scene. A fighter can be removed at any moment: the tool does not wait for the circle to reach them.
        |WHEN: the fighter has dropped out for good — killed, surrendered, fled, carried off, turned to stone. While they can return to the ranks (dying, stunned, bound) — do NOT remove: they stay in the roster, you hand them the turn (`passSpotlight`), and you also play them out, and it is exactly in this turn that their death saving throw is rolled.
        |⚰️ OUT OF THE BATTLE — DOES NOT MEAN OUT OF THE SCENE: the corpse stays ACTIVE, its token stays on the map (a body is a tactical object: people hide behind it, search it, mourn it), the states are not removed from the sheet. Removing a body from the scene is a separate decision and not in battle.
        |The dropping out must be VOICED in the narrative in the same response — otherwise the fighter vanishes from the battle silently.
name: removeFromBattle

description:
⚔️🕵️ Append to the character's COMBAT DOSSIER based on a LIVE battle. The dossier is your working assessment of combat capability (the "⚔️🕵️ CHARACTER COMBAT DOSSIERS" block); the axes by the SHEET are computed by a separate assessor agent (at character creation, at a sheet edit and at the end of a turn if the build changed significantly), while you edit by the FACT seen at the table.

        |When to call:
        |- the battle showed that the assessment does not match reality ("survivability 1.0, yet they are taken down in a round" — lower it);
        |- a concrete vulnerability or technique to remember was revealed ("afraid of fire — checked at the mill", "in a panic forgets the bonus action") — put it into `observation`;
        |- the dossier is marked OUTDATED (the level grew above the assessed one) — recompute the axes.

        |When NOT to call: the character has no dossier at all (created before assessments appeared) — do not invent one on the fly, judge such a character by the sheet, and record the conclusion with `addDecision`. And do not rewrite the dossier "just in case": without a new fact from the battle an edit only makes noise.

        |The axes are OPTIONAL one by one: pass only those you really change (null — the axis stays as it was). `observation` is appended to the list of observations, the previous ones are not erased; a REPEAT of an already recorded observation is dropped — do not rewrite the same fact in other words. This is YOUR working note, and the player does not see it: do not retell the dossier in the narrative, in NPC lines or in orders to specialists.
name: updateCombatAssessment

textId.description: textId of the character whose dossier you are editing.

observation.description: A new observation from live combat in ONE phrase, up to 300 characters ("afraid of fire — checked at the mill"). Appended to the list (a duplicate of a previous one is dropped). null — axes/note only.

durability.description: New SURVIVABILITY rating. The axis scale is 0.0-2.0, where 1.0 = the contribution of a REFERENCE fighter OF THEIR OWN LEVEL on this axis (the level is already built into the scale: a level-1 mage and a level-10 mage can both have damage 1.2). 0.0 — no such axis at all; 0.5 — half as strong as the reference; 1.5+ — the build is tuned to this axis. null — do not change.

damage.description: New DAMAGE-per-round rating. The axis scale is 0.0-2.0, where 1.0 = the contribution of a REFERENCE fighter OF THEIR OWN LEVEL on this axis (the level is already built into the scale: a level-1 mage and a level-10 mage can both have damage 1.2). 0.0 — no such axis at all; 0.5 — half as strong as the reference; 1.5+ — the build is tuned to this axis. null — do not change.

control.description: New CONTROL rating. The axis scale is 0.0-2.0, where 1.0 = the contribution of a REFERENCE fighter OF THEIR OWN LEVEL on this axis (the level is already built into the scale: a level-1 mage and a level-10 mage can both have damage 1.2). 0.0 — no such axis at all; 0.5 — half as strong as the reference; 1.5+ — the build is tuned to this axis. null — do not change.

support.description: New SUPPORT rating. The axis scale is 0.0-2.0, where 1.0 = the contribution of a REFERENCE fighter OF THEIR OWN LEVEL on this axis (the level is already built into the scale: a level-1 mage and a level-10 mage can both have damage 1.2). 0.0 — no such axis at all; 0.5 — half as strong as the reference; 1.5+ — the build is tuned to this axis. null — do not change.

plannerAssessment.description: The new hidden master's note ("Strong: … Weak: … Against: …") IN FULL, replacing the previous one, up to 1200 characters. null — keep the previous one.

description:
⚔️📝 Correct the PLAN of the current battle for a changed situation. The battle plan is a LIVING document: it is persisted with the battle and the NEXT combat turns are run by it. The situation changed (the shield source is destroyed, reinforcements arrived, the party changed its goal, a new facet of the idea was revealed) — correct the plan so that the further battle follows the current design.
        |PARTIAL update: pass ONLY the fields you change — unpassed (null) ones stay as they were. Keep the subordination: the tactical question, the synergies and the world events work for the battle's IDEA, not against it.
        |Works only in an active battle (the battle spec exists).
name: updateEncounterPlan

idea.description: New battle IDEA — why it now exists in the story (what is at stake/what it reveals), if it shifted/deepened. NOT decoration. null — leave untouched.

tacticalQuestion.description: New tactical question — "how it plays" for the current situation ("the shield source is destroyed → now just finish them"). null — leave untouched.

synergies.description: New list of enemy synergies (fully replaces the previous one). null — leave untouched.

worldEventSeeds.description: New list of world-event drafts (fully replaces the previous one). null — leave untouched.

description: Record a finding in the REVIEW phase: concretely, what is violated in the add-on — "crossed the lite boundary: played out mechanics that do not belong to it", "the whisper went out as a public part", "the NPC's answer is not per canon", "a failed roll was played out as a success". Findings are OPEN until rechecked: they hang before your eyes every pass until fixed, and the add-on is not finalized while even one is open. A finding is raised by the RESULT in the snapshot (what landed and what did not), not by the work process. USE ONLY IN THE REVIEW PHASE. Do NOT call transitionTo — the frame will transition itself.
name: addFinding

description.description: Specific description of the violation — what exactly is wrong.

severity.description: Criticality. CRITICAL — must be fixed; HIGH — serious; NORMAL — an improvement.

description: Append a fact to the TURN SUMMARY (a collapsed history feed + material for future chapter compression): if this add-on added an EVENT (not empty chatter) — one factual sentence about what happened. NOT a mandatory step — decide yourself whether the add-on was significant enough; a trivial/clarifying add-on need not be noted. Several calls per pass are concatenated in call order, they do not overwrite each other.
name: appendToSummary

line.description: One factual sentence about the event of this add-on (no speculation, no retelling of lines).

description: ⛔ ONLY IN THE REVIEW PHASE. From REPLY the call returns a refusal: first transitionTo(REVIEW) — and CLOSING THE MOVE IN THE SAME RESPONSE IS IMPOSSIBLE (the transition is applied at the END of the response, so closeMove goes in the NEXT response, already from the review). Close the participant's move: you accepted its playing out, and it is ready to become canon. Call LAST in the response: saving happens at the END of this response — as a single record (the narrative, rolls, sheet changes, decisions, world records). After saving the move is IMMUTABLE: there is nothing left to edit its parts with (updatePart/removePart), and the players will see it immediately. A move can be closed only when the review is clean (no open findings) and everything ordered from the specialists has been played out — otherwise the call will return a refusal with the reason. Then the cycle either passes the turn to the next scene participant or finishes the pass if there is nobody left to move.
name: closeMove

summary.description: One sentence — WHAT happened in this turn (for the context of the pass's next turns; not a retelling of the whole narrative, but the essence of the event).

spendsMove.description: WHETHER THE FIGHTER'S TURN IS SPENT by this move. Works ONLY in battle and ONLY for a fighter who moves on their own (a player without delegation); for a guided one and outside battle the parameter affects nothing — the turn is spent. `true` (default) — something happened in the world: the fighter spent the turn and moves up to their barrier. `false` — THE WORLD STOOD STILL: you answered the player's meta-question ("can I reach it?", "what do I see?", "how does this work by the rules?"), nothing happened, no action was declared — then the turn is NOT spent: the fighter stays in place and keeps the spotlight, no need to hand it out again. Look at the CONTENT of the turn, not its length: any action in the world (a strike, a movement, a spell, a dash, assistance) is `true`, even if described in one line.

description: A "no changes" receipt for the sheet's debt rows: there are no changes for the named rows. The receipt changes nothing in the sheet — it answers for a row on a par with an edit. Cases in which "no changes" is the correct answer: a long rest has begun and not finished; exhaustion is not removed by every rest; a resource whose description says "is not restored by this rest". Rows that are not in the debt presented to you are not closed by the receipt — the answer names them in a separate list.
name: settleMoment

characterTextId.description: textId of the participant whose sheet the receipt is written for.

resourceIds.description: IDs of this sheet's resource rows that have no changes.

all.description: A receipt for ALL the participant's uncovered debt — for every presented row that is still unanswered. Lists are not needed for this.

description: Move to the next phase of the add-on. Call LAST in the response, when the current phase's work is done: the transition is applied at the END of this response, all the other calls of this same response still execute in the current phase (so do not plan work AFTER it expecting the new phase). If some tool of this response returned "ERROR:", the transition is delayed and the turn returns to you in the current phase — first fix the failure.
name: transitionTo
